# E1 (pilot Part A′): family width × steepness on the box — reduced models against the tuned spectral FOM

**Status:** checkpoint report, generated by `make_report.py`; every measured number is read from the collected cell JSONs (registered widths, targets and thresholds are design values) (cells: W40_A1 (W40_A1)); GPU-hours 9.09 of 87 (ledger `runs/GPU-LEDGER.json`). All errors are against the lane's **spectral conditional references** (a labelled lane deviation from the E0 second-order recipe, DESIGN A2.2): $\varepsilon_{\rm ref}$ is a conditional estimate, never a bound. Selection on val32 only; the test-once cohorts are not opened in this report unless stated. Every speed-up $S$ is an upper bound on our speed-up over the tested FOM ladder (a stronger FOM can only lower it), measured on one H200 per cell job.

## Question and stop rule (DESIGN §0, §9, A2.8, A3.3)

On the unit box, for which family width $W$ and steepness level does a reduced model reach $S=t^\ast_{\rm FOM}/t^\ast_{\rm ROM}\ge1$ (and $\ge2$) at matched median and worst error $\tau\in\{1,3,10\}\,\%$?

> Stop the line if every reduced model has $S < 0.5$ at every target on the wide family (W ≥ 0.28 cells). Also stop the bank arm if its projection floor at its own equal-cost size $r_\times$ is above τ in every cell.

## Glossary

- **W**: family width: bump centres are drawn uniformly in a square of side W centred at (0.5, 0.5).
- **A1–A4**: steepness levels: viscosity bands differing by a factor 3 per level; A4 is the steepest.
- **τ**: error target for the median or the worst case over the eligible validation cases of the cell.
- **N, n, tol**: FOM: N − 1 sine modes per direction; n time steps; tol the adaptive local-error tolerance.
- **r, q, tensor, κ, n**: reduced models: r basis functions; q the Gauss points per element of the quadrature rule (or the exact precontracted tensor); κ the ECSW sample size per basis function; n time steps.
- **boundary labels**: the selected FOM configuration sits at the edge of its tested ladder (search truncated).
- **finalist-partial / missing-construction / operator-check-failed**: an arm whose search or construction was incomplete (partial evidence) / produced no valid configuration / whose basis failed its operator checks.
- **arm-unqualified / search-incomplete / timing invalid**: configurations met τ but none passed numerical qualification / the qualification attempt cap was reached / the paired timing failed its validity checks (identical outputs, no compilation, doubled-query check).
- **registered values**: widths, levels, targets and thresholds printed here are design values from DESIGN.md, not measurements; every measured number is read from the cell JSONs.
- **F-SPEC / F-SPEC-AD**: the sine pseudo-spectral full-order solver with fixed / adaptive (step-doubling) ETDRK4 time steps.
- **R-PODG**: POD–Galerkin reduced model (the pilot’s stand-in), Galerkin ETDRK4, exact quadrature tensor or a Gauss rule.
- **R-ECSW**: POD with energy-conserving sampling and weighting (a sparse fitted quadrature).
- **R-TRANS**: static translation approximation: a POD model of centred bumps, decoded shifted to the true centre.
- **B-LSPG / B-E4**: our coordinate-network bank with the incumbent least-squares stepper / the Galerkin ETDRK4 stepper.
- **S**: speed-up = FOM time / reduced-model time at matched error, paired A–B–A timing on one H200; S > 1 means the reduced model is faster.
- **finalist**: the fastest validated configuration of an arm that meets τ and passes numerical qualification (Q1, Q2).
- **arm-censored**: no configuration of the arm reached τ (not speed evidence either way).
- **$r_\times$**: equal-cost size: the largest bank size whose one nonlinear evaluation is no slower than one FOM evaluation.
- **floor**: projection floor: the best possible error of the bank’s first r functions on the reference fields.
- **U, ε_ref**: conditional reference-error allowance and estimate (spectral convergence differences).
- **Q1 / Q2**: numerical qualification: solver/update correctness certificate; quadrature agreement between successive rules.
